ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615, Laws of Hong Kong), Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing (Financial Institution) Rules, Hong Kong Monetary Authority AML/CFT Guideline, the People's Bank of China Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records Preservation (Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024), and the Measures for the Registration of Beneficial Owners of Market Entities (SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong company (or Foreign-Invested Partnership registration certificate if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: Issued and certified by the Hong Kong Companies Registry or authorised certifying officer, then apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong; no consular legalization is required for use in Mainland China because both Hong Kong and Mainland China are part of the same sovereign jurisdiction and cross-border document authentication follows the Arrangement on Mutual Recognition and Assistance in Civil and Commercial Matters, but if used in a non-Apostille Convention state, consular legalization through the Chinese consulate and the destination state consulate applies; never combine both paths sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Current Status
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization by the relevant consulate after authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or its authorised office in Hong Kong; the two authentication paths are mutually exclusive alternatives, not sequential chains.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorising formation of the Mainland China Foreign-Invested Partnership and execution of incorporation documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the Hong Kong parent entity or the authorised partners of the FIP
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarised before a Hong Kong notary public and apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization through the Chinese consulate after notarisation and authentication by the High Court; the two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All founding partners and the FIP legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: the executed partnership agreement must be notarised by a Chinese notary public and apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China or its authorised office, if destined for an Apostille Convention state; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization at the destination country's consulate in China after MFA authentication; never chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the principal settlement bank of the Hong Kong entity or the intended bank account of the FIP
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong or Mainland China (e.g., a commercial bank licensed by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or the National Financial Regulatory Administration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: if addressed to an overseas counterpart and issued by a Hong Kong bank, the bank's signature is notarised and apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong; for non-Apostille states, consular legalization through the foreign consulate after authentication; the two channels are parallel alternatives and must never be combined sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency / Registered Particulars and Directors and Shareholders Register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry or licensed company service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Where required for the mainland registration, the document is produced by the Companies Registry and authenticated under the Hong Kong notary system and then either apostilled by the High Court of Hong Kong for Apostille Convention destinations or consular-legalised through the Chinese consulate and destination consulate for non-member states; parallel paths only.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, limited partners holding at least 25% of capital, legal representatives, and authorised signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence against the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's PEP registers, the United Nations Sanctions Lists, the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and Ministry of Commerce export control and sanctions lists, the U.S. OFAC SDN List and sectoral sanctions, the EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists, INTERPOL notices, and the FATF mutual evaluation data. Screening must be conducted at onboarding, before each capital contribution, at contract signing, and on a continuous risk-based basis at least monthly for all underlying ad traffic suppliers, payment intermediaries, and distribution partners. Any exact or fuzzy match triggers a risk rating review, source-of-wealth investigation, and where required, a suspension of formation and filing of a suspicious transaction report with the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit in Hong Kong and the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring Analysis Center. For a hyper-casual gaming entity with cross-border AdMob and AppLovin payouts, the compliance file must include copies of the sanctions screening logs, PEP declarations, and evidence of independent verification of beneficial ownership through government-owned registries.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) enterprise name registration online platform; for Hong Kong parent, the Hong Kong Companies Registry Cyber Search Centre and Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Foreign-Invested Partnership established in Mainland China must have a Chinese-language name consisting of the administrative division, unique distinctive component, industry or business characteristic, and organisational form, with the Chinese characters selected to avoid identical or confusingly similar names in the SAMR database. The Hong Kong entity name may be registered in English and/or Chinese; where the FIP is formed with foreign investors, the foreign-language name must be submitted as a standardised phonetic or semantic transliteration that does not conflict with the Chinese name, and all transliteration must comply with the Government General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine transliteration standards for English-Chinese names; the four-tier naming convention requires (1) administrative division, (2) trade name, (3) industry description matching ISIC 5820/software publishing, and (4) legal form 'Foreign-Invested Limited Partnership' or 'Foreign-Invested Partnership'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Sensitive words requiring ministerial approval for financial, licensed, or public-interest industries
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the enterprise name reservation by the SAMR online platform, the applicant must first request an administrative reconsideration or appeal through the local SAMR's online complaint channel within 15 working days of the rejection notice. The appeal must restate the exact proposed name, cite the specific reason for rejection, provide evidence of no identical or confusingly similar registered name in the relevant administrative division and industry, and demonstrate compliance with the Regulations on Enterprise Name Registration and the Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships. If the local SAMR upholds the rejection, the applicant may file a second-level reconsideration with the next higher SAMR or, where the rejection involves the Ministry of Commerce approval for restricted industry names, apply for a ministerial pre-approval. The appeal body must issue a written decision within 30 days and any administrative litigation may be commenced in the People's Court after exhaustion of administrative reconsideration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: The local tax authority and the State Administration for Market Regulation generally reject a bare virtual office or commercial mailbox as the sole registered address for a Foreign-Invested Partnership engaged in software publishing and ad-monetised gaming, because the FIP is required to maintain a physical place of business in China, and the industry-specific 'commercial substance' review under the Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships and the tax registration rules demands actual office premises, personnel, servers or contracts within China; banks will refuse to open an operating account for an entity with only a virtual mailbox unless a full lease agreement, utility bill, or property right certificate is provided; a compliant registered address must be a leased physical office, serviced office with dedicated meeting room and staff, or a government-designated incubation address expressly approved for FIP registration, but not a mail-forwarding PO box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Municipal tax authorities and SAMR perform unannounced physical inspections of newly formed foreign-invested partnerships at an estimated 25%-40% probability during the first 12 months if the registered address is in a shared or serviced office, and 5%-15% if the premises are occupied by the partnership alone. The examiner will verify the presence of the registered office signboard, lease documents, fixed assets, staff attendance records, accounting ledgers, and the FIP's operational capacity to publish and monetise games; failure to pass an inspection may result in restoration of the entity to the registry and revocation of the overseas payment-rail registrations with AdMob and AppLovin. Therefore, the entity must keep the lease, utility bills, insurance policy, employment contracts of resident staff, Chinese-language website or app listings, and server logs available at the registered address at all times.
physical_inspection_likelihood_checklist: Registered address signboard matching the approved Chinese enterprise name
Originals of the lease agreement and rent payment receipts
Utility bills under the FIP name or the lessor's name with an explanatory note
Employment contracts and social insurance records of resident staff
Accounting books, bank statements, and tax filing records
Copies of game publishing licences (if any) and ad-network contracts
Minutes of partner meetings and resolutions
Asset list including computers, servers, and office furniture

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap 37), Laws of Hong Kong, sections 4 to 9 and 13; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), sections 5 and 6; Companies Ordinance (Cap 622), Part 2 and Schedule 1, insofar as a corporate general partner is appointed.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Partnerships Section, and the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed with the Companies Registry, together with Form IRBR1 (Application for Business Registration) filed with the Business Registration Office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Limited Partnership Ordinance imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or blocked capital account requirement. The partners may agree cash, property, or services as capital contributions in the Limited Partnership Agreement. A licensed bank may impose internal minimum balances for account opening, but the state does not require any prescribed minimum capital for a Hong Kong limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP OR OF ITS GENERAL PARTNER’S MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE. At a duly convened first meeting of the Board of Directors or management committee of the Partnership held at [●] on [date], it was resolved unanimously as follows. 1. RESOLVED that the formation of the Partnership as a Hong Kong limited partnership under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap 37), and the registration of its business under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310), be and the same are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in every respect; and the General Partner be and is hereby authorised to execute, deliver, notarise, and file all forms, statements, consents, and statutory documents necessary to perfect such registration, and to pay all applicable government fees and professional charges. 2. RESOLVED that the capital of the Partnership set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement, namely the capital contributions subscribed by the General Partner in the amount of HK$[●] and by the Limited Partners in the aggregate amount of HK$[●], be and the same are hereby subscribed, accepted, credited to the capital accounts of the respective partners, and recorded in the register of partners; and no such contribution shall be withdrawn or repaid except in strict compliance with the Partnership Agreement and the Limited Partnership Ordinance. 3. RESOLVED that the registered office and principal place of business of the Partnership within Hong Kong be and is hereby established at [●], Hong Kong, and that the Partnership be authorised to maintain its statutory records, minute books, registers, bank account records, and corporate seal at such address. 4. RESOLVED that the General Partner be and is hereby authorised to open, maintain, and operate corporate bank accounts with such licensed banks in Hong Kong as may be selected by the General Partner, and that any two of [●], [●], and [●] be and are hereby appointed as joint authorised signatories for the purpose of signing all cheques, banking mandates, foreign-currency settlement instructions, AdMob payout receipts, AppLovin payout receipts, and other financial documents. 5. RESOLVED that [●] be and is hereby appointed as the Designated Representative for Business Registration purposes, [●] be and is hereby appointed as the Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer, and [●] be and is hereby appointed as the Statutory Compliance Officer of the Partnership, each with full power to file all necessary returns and to represent the Partnership before the Companies Registry, the Inland Revenue Department, and other competent authorities. 6. RESOLVED FURTHER that all actions taken and documents executed prior to this resolution for or on behalf of the Partnership in connection with its formation are hereby ratified, adopted, and confirmed as acts of the Partnership; and the partners, officers, and authorised signatories are directed to carry out the foregoing resolutions and to do all things necessary or incidental to give effect thereto.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Legal Name Clearance, Limited Partnership Agreement Execution, and Foreign Investor Eligibility Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Partnerships Section, via the Integrated Companies Registry Information System and e-Registry portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a live Companies Registry name search to confirm that the proposed partnership name does not conflict with an existing legal entity or reserved name and does not contain any prohibited or offensive word. Prepare and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement stating the identity of the general partner, the identities and capital commitments of the limited partners, profit-sharing ratios, admission and withdrawal mechanics, and governing law. If any partner is a foreign natural person, obtain a certified copy of the passport and proof of residential address; if any partner is a foreign body corporate, obtain a certificate of good standing and a notarized board or authority resolution approving participation. Notarisation of the Limited Partnership Agreement is not mandated by Hong Kong law, but notarise the document if the foreign regulator or bank requires it for anti-money-laundering purposes.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name in English and Chinese, if applicable
Draft Limited Partnership Agreement
Certified passport copies and residential address proofs of all natural partners
Certificate of good standing and board resolution of any corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
Notarised power of attorney or authority resolution, if a representative signs on behalf of a foreign partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search reveals a conflict or the Registrar queries partner identity, promptly revise the proposed name or submit a statutory declaration and a supporting counsel opinion distinguishing the proposed name from existing names. No name refusal is final, and a fresh application may be made with corrected particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership with the Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Partnerships Section, via the Integrated Companies Registry Information System.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form LP1 electronically or in paper to the Partnerships Section of the Companies Registry, attaching the certified Limited Partnership Agreement and the identity documents of all partners. The general partner must sign Form LP1 and confirm that the partnership contains at least one general partner with unconditional liability and at least one limited partner. Foreign ownership is expressly permissible. Pay the prescribed registration fee, and the Registrar will examine the particulars for consistency with the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap 37) and issue the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. Upon registration, the partnership obtains juridical capacity for statutory purposes, and the general partner must ensure that the particulars of limited partners are not published in a manner constituting an offer to the public.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 signed by the general partner
Certified copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Name clearance certificate or name search result
Identity documents of the general and limited partners
Consent to act as general partner, if applicable
Registration fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried as defective or suspended, respond in writing to the Registrar within the stated requisition period, provide certified English translations or missing consents, and amend Form LP1 for resubmission. A rejection may be cured by rectification and a new submission without prejudice to the partnership’s intended formation date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR, through the IRD Business Registration online portal or counter service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month after the Companies Registry registration, apply to the Business Registration Office of the Inland Revenue Department using Form IRBR1. Attach the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership and the identity documents of the partners. Pay the annual business registration fee and the protection levy, and the office will issue the Business Registration Certificate. Display the certificate at the registered office or principal place of business. For a pure digital publisher falling within ISIC 5820, no sectoral licence is required; the Business Registration Certificate constitutes the only general operating permit. The partnership must update the business registration within one month of any change in name, nature of business, address, or partners.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR1 (Application for Business Registration)
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Identity documents of all partners and the designated representative
Lease agreement or landlord consent for the registered office, if any
Business Registration fee and levy payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Inland Revenue Department queries the application, provide the Companies Registry certificate and a clear description of the digital publishing business model. Late application liabilities may be mitigated by showing a reasonable excuse and paying any assessed fees, subject to the Business Registration Ordinance appeal and waiver procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office, Statutory Registers, and Appointment of Statutory Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partnership registered office in Hong Kong; any change of particulars must be notified to the Companies Registry and the Inland Revenue Department.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the registered office by executing a lease or obtaining landlord consent, and file the registered office and principal place of business particulars with the Companies Registry and the Inland Revenue Department. Prepare the statutory register of partners, minute book, and capital account ledgers and keep them at the registered office. Hold the first board meeting and pass the first board resolution appointing the Designated Representative for Business Registration, the Anti-Money Laundering Compliance Officer, and the Statutory Compliance Officer. Ensure that each officer executes a signed consent to act and that the appointment is recorded in the statutory registers. Where the partnership collects personal data in the course of gaming operations, appoint a data privacy officer and adopt a privacy policy compliant with the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap 486) as an internal governance measure.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the first board resolution
Limited Partnership Agreement and any amendments
Lease agreement or registered office consent form
Register of partners with capital contribution entries
Signed consents to act from all statutory officers
Data privacy policy, if personal data is processed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are found to be incomplete, cure the deficiency by preparing corrected minutes and consents, and file any late notification with the Companies Registry or Inland Revenue Department under the applicable reasonable-excuse provisions. Ensure that all recorded dates are accurate and supported by board authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Activation and AdMob and AppLovin Payment Rail Integration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A licensed bank in Hong Kong authorized under the Banking Ordinance (Cap 155), selected by the General Partner.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the selected licensed Hong Kong bank the certified first board resolution, the Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership, the Business Registration Certificate, the Limited Partnership Agreement, and a certified beneficial ownership declaration. The bank will perform know-your-client, source-of-wealth, sanctions, and politically exposed person screening. Complete the account opening forms, specimen signature cards, and banking mandate; any two authorised signatories must execute the mandate. Instruct the bank to designate the account as the dedicated collection account for AdMob and AppLovin payouts, and to require dual approval for all outbound transfers. If the bank requests additional corroboration, provide notarised corporate documents or an updated beneficial ownership schedule.
required_dossiers: Certified first board resolution
Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Beneficial ownership declaration
Source of funds statement
Specimen signatures and executed banking mandate
Sanctions and politically exposed person declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the application or imposes additional KYC conditions, provide supplementary source-of-funds evidence and a certified organisational chart. The partnership may approach another licensed Hong Kong bank, and unreasonable refusals may be raised through the bank’s internal complaint procedure before engaging the Hong Kong Monetary Authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable – no industrial licensing board, municipal manufacturing agency, or factories department has jurisdiction over a pure digital publisher under ISIC 5820.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable – no sectoral operating licence beyond the general Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310); platform-specific requirements from Google Play, Apple App Store, AdMob, and AppLovin are contractual, not state-issued permits.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR – Not Applicable / Not Triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable – no designated project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap 499); pure software publishing and hyper-casual game distribution involve no construction, physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing works.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation; the partnership’s digital operations rely on cloud infrastructure provided by third-party data centres, whose environmental compliance is outside the partnership’s direct operational control.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – no Civil Defense fire permit, Dangerous Goods Licence, or structural load certificate is required for virtual digital publishing operations. If the partnership leases a physical office in Hong Kong, the landlord or building owner must provide fire service installation certification under the Fire Services Ordinance (Cap 95) and compliance under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap 123), and the partnership should obtain an occupational safety risk assessment for its office premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic portal: China Electronic Taxpayer Hall (e-Taxation) on the official STA website at www.chinatax.gov.cn. For Hong Kong SAR application, the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) and its eTax portal at www.ird.gov.hk constitute the separate competent authority for Hong Kong profits tax and business registration, but Hong Kong has no VAT/GST authority function.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing or joining a Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) must first complete SAMR establishment registration, which automatically issues the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) that serves as the taxpayer identification number for all PRC tax purposes. Within 30 days of issuance of the business license, the FIP must complete tax registration with the STA through the Electronic Taxpayer Hall, at which point the USCC is activated for VAT, corporate income tax, withholding, and invoice issuance. Foreign non-resident partners that themselves have no fixed place of business in China and derive PRC-source income are subject to source withholding registration administered by the FIP as withholding agent, and no separate VAT identification number is required unless the non-resident partner directly supplies taxable services in China. If the foreign entity is a Hong Kong entity, it must separately obtain a Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate from the IRD and, if taxable, a Profits Tax file reference under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, but no VAT/GST number is issued in Hong Kong. VAT registration for the FIP is entity-level and does not flow through to partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible – the PRC FIP is tax transparent for corporate income tax; partnership profits, gains, losses, and credits are allocated to the partners under the Partnership Enterprise Law and PRC partnership taxation rules, and each partner is taxed on its allocated share at its applicable resident or non-resident rate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not operate a check-the-box election for partnerships; a Chinese FIP is mandatorily treated as a pass-through entity. PRC hybrid mismatch rules under the corporate income tax special tax adjustment framework apply to deny inconsistent tax outcomes where a foreign partner jurisdiction treats the FIP as an opaque entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) in mainland China; Hong Kong SAR imposes no VAT, GST, or general sales tax and relies on profits tax and duties on specified dutiable commodities only.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mainland China: no VAT registration turnover threshold exists; all FIPs must complete tax registration within 30 days of establishment. The compulsory VAT general taxpayer registration threshold is annual taxable turnover above CNY 5,000,000 on a rolling 12-month basis. Hong Kong SAR: no threshold applies because no VAT/GST regime exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory electronic invoice regime for VAT taxpayers: all VAT invoices must be issued through the STA national electronic invoice platform, with real-time data transmission to the Golden Tax Phase IV supervision system. The platform validates each invoice by a unique invoice code and digital anti-fraud stamping; taxpayers integrate through the Tax Control U-Key or full-digital e-invoice API. E-invoices must be electronically archived and are subject to instant clearance surveillance. Hong Kong SAR has no VAT and therefore no fiscal clearance, e-invoicing mandate, or tax authority invoice stamping; Hong Kong commercial invoices are ordinary trading documents without clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under China's VAT export regime, 0% VAT zero-rating applies to (i) physical goods exported out of PRC customs territory, provided the customs export declaration names the FIP as exporter; (ii) qualifying exported services consumed entirely offshore, including ad-monetized hyper-casual game publishing revenue derived from overseas end-users and paid by non-resident ad networks such as AdMob and AppLovin, where the service recipient is outside China and the services are not physically rendered in mainland China; and (iii) software-related cross-border taxable services within the statutory zero-rating/exemption list. The FIP must prove commercial reality through contracts, offshore consumption, foreign exchange receipt, and service delivery evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Goods Declaration / Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading (or Air Waybill as equivalent transport document)
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC); in mainland China, the Cross-Border Receipts and Payments Declaration issued by the receiving bank is the statutory equivalent

Export sales contract, commercial invoice, packing list, and for digital services: signed offshore service agreement, AdMob/AppLovin payout statements, user distribution metrics, and evidence that the game services were consumed outside PRC customs territory
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA may retrospectively disallow export zero-rating and claw back VAT refunds where the FIP fails to substantiate physical export, foreign exchange repatriation within the 180-day statutory window, or offshore consumption of digital services. Under the Law of the PRC on the Administration of Tax Collection, fraudulent export refund claims attract recovery of the full unpaid or refunded VAT plus late-payment interest and surcharge, administrative penalties of between 50% and 500% of the evaded tax, and, under the Criminal Law, export tax fraud liability including fines and imprisonment up to life. Taxpayers are also placed on enhanced scrutiny profiles, suspended from export refund facilitation for extended periods, and subjected to retroactive audits covering prior filing years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China as the upstream controlling authority for mainland Chinese cross-border flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region operates a separate monetary and financial system within the People's Republic of China. There is no foreign exchange control regime administered by the People's Bank of China inside Hong Kong. The HKMA maintains the Linked Exchange Rate System, allowing currency convertibility for both current-account and capital-account items without prior approval. The Hong Kong dollar is freely convertible; foreign exchange receipts and capital inflows may be retained, repatriated, or invested without surrender requirements. Profit and dividend remittance from a Hong Kong treasury booking centre or partnership to non-resident partners is unrestricted, subject only to tax compliance and AML/KYC checks. However, if the ultimate financial owner is a mainland Chinese foreign-invested partnership or a Chinese investor injecting funds from the mainland, cross-border RMB/USD flows are subject to SAFE direct investment registration, foreign debt registration, capital-account supervision, and bank receipt confirmation. Non-resident partners in Hong Kong can freely subscribe capital in HKD, USD, or offshore CNH, but any corresponding capital injection from mainland China into the international structure requires ODI/FDI registration, tax declaration, and a compliant payment trail before profits are repatriated. In short, convertibility is complete at the Hong Kong treasury layer, while mainland controls continue to apply as upstream regulatory gates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion ratio applies in Hong Kong. Export proceeds from the hyper-casual games business, including AdMob and AppLovin payouts, may be credited directly to a multi-currency operating account and held in USD, HKD, or any freely convertible currency. For mainland-connected export or service income, SAFE requires the enterprise to declare authenticity, settle collected foreign exchange through a designated bank, and submit export/transaction documents under the current-account verification system; surplus proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the enterprise's discretion within the verified quota.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited (HSBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / RMB and CNH Operational Clearing Account
Operational Multi-Currency Account / FX Hedging Collateral Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (Asia) Limited (ICBC Asia)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility for fintech EMIs is High only as an ancillary collection or payout rail for the AdMob/AppLovin revenue stream, but Low as the sole infrastructure for capital escrow and treasury clearing. A legally viable EMI must hold a Hong Kong Stored Value Facility (SVF) licence under the Payment Systems and Stored Value Facilities Ordinance or a Money Service Operator (MSO) licence under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (AMLO). Such EMIs are not deposit-taking institutions and cannot provide the same credit, documentary trade, or capital-verification functions as Tier-1 licensed banks. Offshore digital EMIs without a Hong Kong licence are legally barred from soliciting or maintaining Hong Kong jurisdictional treasury accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: HKMA does not statutorily require physical branch attendance for account opening, but Tier-1 bank KYC policies for a newly formed non-resident partnership generally require the general partner, an authorized signatory, and at least one ultimate beneficial owner to appear in branch or complete an HKMA-bank-approved video interview with a relationship manager. Remote consular proxy opening is rarely accepted because AMLO requires independent verification of beneficial ownership and identity; a workable path is a video-KYC interview supplemented by notarized corporate documents, certified passport copies, and a solicitor-issued opinion on the partnership's existence and capacity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly registered partnership with no operating history and a multi-layer GP/LP ownership chain spanning China and Hong Kong.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Registration (CR), Business Registration Certificate (BRC), executed partnership agreement, register of partners, register of charges, significant controllers register / Register of Beneficial Owners, 24-month supporting bank statements from existing investors, notarized passports and residential utility bills of all UBOs, source-of-funds declaration, GP indemnity confirming no anonymous shell owners, and a corporate structure chart tracing each 25% or greater beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-ticket AdMob/AppLovin micro-payouts create an aggregated settlement pattern that appears similar to unlicensed money service business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform settlement statements from AdMob and AppLovin, app-store analytics and payout reports, user acquisition campaign invoices and receipts, a signed contract with each ad network, a revenue reconciliation ledger mapping micro-payouts to game titles, privacy and data protection compliance documentation, and a written funds-flow narrative demonstrating that the partnership is the beneficial recipient of software publishing revenue rather than a payment processor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from mainland China into the Hong Kong partnership may be improperly classified as a non-compliant outbound remittance or disguised foreign exchange arbitrage.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE outbound direct investment registration certificate for the Chinese investor, board resolution of each investing entity, partnership interest subscription agreement, bank foreign exchange transaction receipt with the correct BOP purpose code for direct investment/partnership capital, FIRS foreign investor registration confirmation, tax registration proof, and a licensed solicitor's opinion confirming the capital contribution is lawful and non-convertible for prohibited purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners or the general partner are Chinese nationals or PRC-domiciled entities with potential PEP, sanctions, or unreported offshore asset exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP and sanctions self-declaration, World-Check/Refinitiv negative-media and sanctions screening report, tax residence certificates for China and Hong Kong, two-year individual income tax returns, wealth provenance evidence including salary, dividends and property sale records, notarized Chinese police background certificate where required, and a senior management declaration that no politically exposed person controls the partnership without enhanced due diligence.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital from mainland China to the Hong Kong treasury structure should be routed as lawful outbound direct investment: the Chinese investor first completes SAFE registration and obtains the bank-issued outward remittance certificate, then remits through SWIFT MT103 (USD/HKD) or CIPS (CNY) using the BOP purpose code for direct investment in partnership capital (6210 series). The Hong Kong receiving bank credits a designated capital subscription or escrow sub-account. Hong Kong itself does not require capital verification, but where the counterpart is a mainland foreign-invested partnership, the receiving bank on the China side requires FDIR registration, a foreign exchange transaction receipt, and an accountant's capital contribution certificate to support future profit remittances.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement for trade and operational disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for direct payments to contractors, ad-technology platforms, app-store payment providers, and FX counterparties; Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 for physical goods or warehousing equipment; and Documentary Collections under URC522 for lower-value invoice-based transactions not requiring LC protection. Recurring AdMob/AppLovin revenue should be collected through dedicated USD/CNH virtual accounts integrated via the bank's API, while outward disbursements for user-acquisition campaigns should be batched through the multi-currency operating account to minimize FX cost and maintain an auditable trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards between USD, HKD, EUR, and offshore CNH with bank-committed credit lines
Vanilla FX options and option spreads executed under an ISDA/CSA agreement
Cross-currency swaps for converting USD/HKD funding into CNH or CNY exposure
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNH/USD for mainland China-related cash flows when physical CNY delivery is not available
Currency swap and rolling spot contracts with HKMA-authorized licensed banks for treasury liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate Renewal (Business Registration Ordinance, Cap.310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: renewal must be completed on or before the expiry date stated on the current certificate; the IRD issues a renewal notice approximately one month before each anniversary.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the certificate lapses, carrying on business without a valid business registration is an offence subject to a fine of up to HK$5,000 and six months' imprisonment. Late renewal may be accepted within 30 days after expiry; after that, the Business Registration Record may be administratively de-activated and a fresh registration is required. No Companies Registry strike-off applies to the partnership itself, but continued non-renewal eliminates the entity's lawful trading posture.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return - Partnership (Form BIR52) and Supporting Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month from the date of issue of the return. IRD issues partnership Profits Tax Returns on a staggered basis after the close of the year of assessment ending 31 March; an authorized tax representative may obtain an extension for e-filing of up to one month from the original due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file without reasonable excuse attracts a maximum fine of HK$10,000 on conviction and, if undercharged tax results, an additional penalty of up to three times the tax undercharged. The IRD may issue an estimated assessment, and unpaid tax is subject to a 5% surcharge in the first six-month period and a further 10% surcharge in the second, with enforced collection through the District Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and Form IR56B for each Employee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the due date stated in the return, normally within one month of the IRD issue date of 1 April for the tax year ended 31 March; a nil return must still be filed if the partnership has no employees. On cessation of business, the return must be filed within 30 days of cessation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence with a maximum fine of HK$10,000; negligence or intentional understatement of remuneration may expose the employer to an additional penalty of up to three times the tax undercharged. Persistent non-compliance can lead to estimated tax assessments and prosecution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Statutory Books Maintenance Confirmation (internal corporate secretarial deliverable submitted to the Managing Partner/General Partner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Managing Partner / Corporate Secretarial Agent; no government filing, documented internally for governance and UBO control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually not later than six months after the financial year end and before the Profits Tax Return filing date, covering the Register of Members (Partners), Register of Directors/General Partners, Register of Charges/Mortgages, minute book, business registration certificate, and Significant Controllers Register where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of adequate statutory registers is a governance deficiency. If a corporate partner is a Hong Kong company under Cap.622, register-keeping failures may attract fines under the Companies Ordinance; it may also be an administrative strike-off ground for that corporate partner and impairs the 30-day share transfer reporting window.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a Hong Kong private company or private corporate group, an independent certified CPA audit is mandatory unless the entity qualifies as a small private company under Companies Ordinance (Cap.622). A small private company satisfies at least two of the following three thresholds in the relevant financial year: (i) annual revenue not exceeding HK$10,000,000 (approximately USD 1,282,000); (ii) balance-sheet total

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% PRC Corporate Income Tax for corporate partners; 16.5% Hong Kong Profits Tax for corporate partners; 0% at FIP entity level (partnership pass-through)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: High-New Technology Enterprise 15%; Key Software Enterprise 10%; qualified R&D super-deduction 100%; Greater Bay Area encouraged-industry 15%; free-trade zone and Qianhai/Hengqin preferential regimes; Hong Kong territorial-source profits tax exemption for qualifying offshore passive income (subject to ESR)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Return (Form A100000) with partnership pass-through schedules and non-resident withholding report; filed via State Taxation Administration e-Tax / Electronic Taxation Bureau portal; Hong Kong Profits Tax Return Form BIR52 for the partnership (if HK partnership filing) filed via IRD eTax/e-filing
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly CIT prepayments; non-resident WHT at source)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: CIT annual settlement due within 5 months after fiscal year-end (May 31); quarterly prepayments within 15 days after quarter-end; non-resident WHT remittance and return due within 7 days of payment/remittance

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification, legal form and tax residence
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify FIP as transparent partnership; disclose each partner as reporting person; for the Hong Kong partner, provide HK Tax Residency Certificate, HK Business Registration number and FATCA/CRS self-certification if claiming treaty benefits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business income (hyper-casual game ad monetization revenue)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report global gross receipts from AdMob, AppLovin and other ad-network contracts; exclude pass-through ad-tech platform fees only if they satisfy expense substantiation; China-sourced income must be disclosed separately from extraterritorial HK-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales and game content development costs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible costs include engine licences, SDK fees, software development and cloud hosting; intercompany royalty or service payments are deductible only if arm's length and supported by transfer pricing documentation; a non-resident vendor with no PE in China may need WHT on fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating, selling, administrative and tax expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses to partners consistently with the partnership agreement; management fees to HK parent are non-deductible unless economically substantive and arm's length; withholding on cross-border service fees may apply under service PE rules if the HK party has tested presence in China.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current-year partnership taxable income and profit allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute partnership taxable income as if a Chinese resident taxpayer, then allocate to each partner according to the partnership agreement; do not net losses of one partner against another; non-resident corporate partner's allocated China-source income is subject to PRC WHT at 10% or reduced DTA rate at the time the income is attributable and remitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding tax, DTA and beneficial ownership schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim Mainland-Hong Kong DTA relief only after obtaining a valid HK Tax Residency Certificate and completing the treaty benefit self-declaration; maintain beneficial ownership evidence showing the HK partner has full power to dispose of the income and no conduit arrangement; failing CIGA review automatically reverts to statutory 10% WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments, foreign tax credit and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply PRC tax loss carryforward of 5 years at partner level; credit Hong Kong Profits Tax paid on the same income against PRC CIT up to the PRC tax attributable to that income; no credit is allowed for taxes that were avoided through sham structures.

The managing general partner or director must sign under personal liability; false allocation, fraudulent invoices or undisclosed offshore payment routes trigger the penalties in the fatal red flags section.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: TCAL imposes fine up to RMB 10,000 and daily late payment surcharge of 0.05% of unpaid tax; underpayment from misreporting: 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax; criminal tax evasion under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201 applies to amounts above statutory thresholds and can result in up to 7 years imprisonment plus fines; Hong Kong IRD late filing may impose HK$10,000 default penalties and an additional assessed tax up to 100% for fraudulent or negligent returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% PRC statutory WHT on China-source dividends and non-resident partner profit allocations that are China-source; 0% Hong Kong dividends because Hong Kong has no dividend withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Under the Mainland-Hong Kong Arrangement, the beneficial owner must obtain a HK Tax Residency Certificate from IRD, submit the treaty benefit self-declaration to the PRC withholding agent or tax authority, disclose the 25% shareholding/interest structure, and evidence that substantive economic activities (CIGA) are performed in Hong Kong; the PRC tax authority may require an enterprise-level beneficial ownership determination and DTA claim before applying the 5% dividend/7% interest/royalty rates; all documentation is required at or before the withholding date and must be retained for at least 10 years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory PRC WHT is 10% for both royalties and interest; under the Mainland-HK DTA the gross-basis treaty ceiling is 7% for interest and 7% for royalties (or 5% for royalties connected with industrial, commercial or scientific equipment) if the beneficial owner qualifies and the payments are made for genuine commercial contracts.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 100 million annual related-party transactions triggers Local File; RMB 1 billion triggers Master File; consolidated group revenue of RMB 5.5 billion triggers CbC Report; Hong Kong TP documentation required when related-party transactions exceed the IRD materiality threshold and IRD forms are requested.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: PRC GAAR at EIT Law Art. 47 and tax administration rules allow recharacterization of transactions lacking commercial substance; for a China-HK structure, the HK partner must satisfy Hong Kong Economic Substance Regulations where applicable and demonstrate that CIGA for hyper-casual gaming — including ad-network contract negotiation, game IP ownership decisions, and server/revenue control — are performed by qualified personnel in Hong Kong; empty-box HK partners will be denied DTA benefits and may be collapsed into the PRC taxable entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and false pass-through allocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP records China-source ad-monetization income, pays or attributes no PRC income tax to the non-resident corporate partner, and remits profits without CIT withholding or by classifying profits falsely as non-taxable guaranteed payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Tax Collection and Administration Law Art. 63: fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax plus daily 0.05% late surcharge; if the fraudulent return is criminalized under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201, imprisonment up to 7 years and fines for amounts considered large.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner or director who signed the false return is jointly and severally liable for restitution of the unpaid tax and penalties; courts may pierce the FIP/HK veil upon finding the partnership was a mere instrumentality; personal travel bans, asset freezes, property seizures and Social Credit blacklisting apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong partner has no staff, office or decision-making in HK; it is interposed solely to convert 10% China-source royalty or dividend income into a 5% or 7% DTA-reduced rate while the actual economic owner remains a PRC-based founder or foreign principal.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SAT Announcement 2018 No. 9 denies treaty benefits for non-beneficial-owner conduits; EIT Law Art. 47 GAAR recharacterizes the scheme and imposes statutory 10% WHT plus surcharges and 50%-500% evasion penalties; serious abuse can trigger criminal fraud prosecution under PRC Criminal Law Art. 201/205.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the sham HK holding company bear personal civil restitution exposure; the corporate protection is lost where the entity is found to be a facade; directors can be denied exit from China, have assets frozen, be blacklisted on the integrated social credit system, and be personally jailed for deliberate treaty-shopping fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: AdMob/AppLovin payouts are routed directly to a partner's private offshore bank account, bypassing the FIP's books, without customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting or cross-border payment declarations; payment records are deliberately fragmented to avoid tax and AML thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law imposes fines up to RMB 5 million on the institution and up to RMB 500,000 on responsible persons for serious AML violations; Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (Cap. 615) imposes fines up to HK$1 million and imprisonment up to 7 years; PRC Criminal Law Art. 191 money-laundering penalties reach 10 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the managing partner are personally liable for AML compliance failures; regulators may pierce the partnership to recover laundered funds, impose civil penalties, issue travel bans (exit denial), blacklist the directors, and convict them for money laundering where the payment routing was knowingly designed to evade tax or sanctions.
